svg.title: Where DevOps came from: a timeline from 2001 to 2024
svg.desc: A vertical timeline. 2001: the Agile Manifesto is signed at Snowbird, Utah, valuing iterative development and close customer collaboration. 2003: Ben Treynor Sloss starts the Google production team that grows into Site Reliability Engineering. 2008: Patrick Debois presents agile infrastructure ideas at the Agile 2008 conference in Toronto. 2009: at Velocity, John Allspaw and Paul Hammond give the talk 10+ Deploys Per Day: Dev and Ops Cooperation at Flickr. 2009: the first devopsdays is held in Ghent, Belgium, on 30 and 31 October, organized by Patrick Debois. 2010: John Willis summarizes DevOps as CAMS, and Jez Humble and David Farley publish Continuous Delivery. 2012: Gene Kim describes the Three Ways of flow, feedback, and continual learning. 2013: The Phoenix Project by Kim, Behr, and Spafford. 2014: DORA's research program begins measuring software delivery performance. 2016: The DevOps Handbook by Kim, Humble, Debois, and Willis. 2018: Accelerate by Forsgren, Humble, and Kim explains the research behind DORA's metrics. 2023 and 2024: DORA renames mean time to recover to failed deployment recovery time and adds deployment rework rate. Colors mark practice and community, operations at Google, books and models, and research and measurement.

g.text: Agile Manifesto (Snowbird, Utah): iterative development and close customer collaboration
Ben Treynor Sloss starts the Google production team that grows into SRE
Patrick Debois presents agile infrastructure ideas at Agile 2008 in Toronto
Velocity: Allspaw and Hammond, "10+ Deploys Per Day: Dev and Ops Cooperation at Flickr"
First devopsdays in Ghent, Belgium (30-31 October), organized by Patrick Debois
John Willis summarizes DevOps as CAMS; Humble and Farley publish Continuous Delivery
Gene Kim describes the Three Ways: flow, feedback, and continual learning
The Phoenix Project, a novel about IT and DevOps, by Kim, Behr, and Spafford
DORA's research program begins measuring software delivery performance
The DevOps Handbook by Kim, Humble, Debois, and Willis
Accelerate by Forsgren, Humble, and Kim explains the research behind DORA's metrics
DORA renames MTTR to failed deployment recovery time and adds deployment rework rate
DevOps began as a practitioner movement in 2008-2009; books and DORA's research then gave it shape.
